PLAN "Upper Body Strength, Cardio, Mobility & Body Recomposition for Climber with Shoulder Impingement"
TYPE workout
VISIBILITY public

GOALS
  GOAL primary strength:
    name "Upper body strength in pain-free range"
  GOAL secondary body_recomposition:
    name "Body recomposition (fat loss, muscle gain)"
  GOAL secondary endurance:
    name "Cardiovascular endurance for long climbing days"
  GOAL secondary climbing_specific:
    name "Climbing-specific grip and movement prep"
  GOAL secondary mobility:
    name "Restore and maintain upper body and shoulder mobility"

SUMMARY
  duration: 12 weeks
  frequency: 4 sessions/week (2 upper body strength, 1 cardio, 1 full body fun finisher in Phase 1-2; 2 upper body strength/climbing, 1 cardio, 1 full body fun finisher in Phase 3)
  structure:
    - Phase 1 (Weeks 1-4): Foundation — upper body strength (pain-free range), mobility, moderate cardio, full body fun finisher
    - Phase 2 (Weeks 5-8): Progression — increased intensity/volume, continued mobility, longer cardio, full body fun finisher
    - Phase 3 (Weeks 9-12): Climbing Prep & Peak — high intensity, hangboard, climbing-specific core, mobility, peaking for trip, full body fun finisher
  key_elements:
    - All pressing/pulling in pain-free, non-overhead range
    - No overhead loading (no overhead_press, military_press, etc)
    - Mobility work in every session (shoulder, chest, lat, spine, neck)
    - Hangboard and climbing-specific core in Phase 3
    - Cardio 1x/week (progressing in duration/intensity)
    - Saturday "Full Body Fun Finisher" (goblet_squat, step_up, push_up, inverted_row, farmers_walk, russian_twist)
    - Nutrition plan for body recomposition (mild deficit, high protein, nutrient-dense, hydration)
    - RPE-based progression, peaking in final weeks
    - All exercises selected for safety with subacromial impingement

NUTRITION
  STRATEGY body_recomposition:
    calories:
      target: "mild deficit (approx. 250-350 kcal below maintenance)"
      notes: "Adjust based on progress and energy levels. Avoid aggressive deficits to support muscle retention."
    protein:
      target: "1.6..2.2 g/kg bodyweight per day"
      notes: "Aim for high-quality protein sources at each meal."
    carbohydrates:
      target: "moderate"
      notes: "Prioritize complex carbs around training sessions for energy and recovery."
    fats:
      target: "balance remainder of calories"
      notes: "Include healthy fats from nuts, seeds, olive oil, fatty fish."
    meal_timing:
      notes: "Distribute protein evenly across 3..5 meals per day. Include a protein-rich meal/snack within 2 hours post-training."
    hydration:
      notes: "Aim for 2..3L water per day. Increase intake with activity and in hot weather."
    micronutrients:
      notes: "Emphasize vegetables, fruits, and whole foods for vitamins and minerals. Consider vitamin D and iron status if plant-based."
    supplements:
      notes: "Consider whey protein, creatine monohydrate, and a multivitamin if dietary intake is insufficient. Consult with a healthcare provider before starting supplements."

PLAN "Upper Body Strength, Cardio, Mobility & Body Recomposition for Climber with Shoulder Impingement"
TYPE workout
VISIBILITY public

GOALS
  GOAL primary strength:
    name "Upper body strength in pain-free range"
  GOAL secondary body_recomposition:
    name "Body recomposition (fat loss, muscle gain)"
  GOAL secondary endurance:
    name "Cardiovascular endurance for long climbing days"
  GOAL secondary climbing_specific:
    name "Climbing-specific grip and movement prep"
  GOAL secondary mobility:
    name "Restore and maintain upper body and shoulder mobility"

SUMMARY
  duration: 12 weeks
  frequency: 4 sessions/week (2 upper body strength, 1 cardio, 1 full body fun finisher in Phase 1-2; 2 upper body strength/climbing, 1 cardio, 1 full body fun finisher in Phase 3)
  structure:
    - Phase 1 (Weeks 1-4): Foundation — upper body strength (pain-free range), mobility, moderate cardio, full body fun finisher
    - Phase 2 (Weeks 5-8): Progression — increased intensity/volume, continued mobility, longer cardio, full body fun finisher
    - Phase 3 (Weeks 9-12): Climbing Prep & Peak — high intensity, hangboard, climbing-specific core, mobility, peaking for trip, full body fun finisher
  key_elements:
    - All pressing/pulling in pain-free, non-overhead range
    - No overhead loading (no overhead_press, military_press, etc)
    - Mobility work in every session (shoulder, chest, lat, spine, neck)
    - Hangboard and climbing-specific core in Phase 3
    - Cardio 1x/week (progressing in duration/intensity)
    - Saturday "Full Body Fun Finisher" (goblet_squat, step_up, push_up, inverted_row, farmers_walk, russian_twist)
    - Nutrition plan for body recomposition (mild deficit, high protein, nutrient-dense, hydration)
    - RPE-based progression, peaking in final weeks
    - All exercises selected for safety with subacromial impingement

NUTRITION
  STRATEGY body_recomposition:
    calories:
      target: "mild deficit (approx. 250-350 kcal below maintenance)"
      notes: "Adjust based on progress and energy levels. Avoid aggressive deficits to support muscle retention."
    protein:
      target: "1.6..2.2 g/kg bodyweight per day"
      notes: "Aim for high-quality protein sources at each meal."
    carbohydrates:
      target: "moderate"
      notes: "Prioritize complex carbs around training sessions for energy and recovery."
    fats:
      target: "balance remainder of calories"
      notes: "Include healthy fats from nuts, seeds, olive oil, fatty fish."
    meal_timing:
      notes: "Distribute protein evenly across 3..5 meals per day. Include a protein-rich meal/snack within 2 hours post-training."
    hydration:
      notes: "Aim for 2..3L water per day. Increase intake with activity and in hot weather."
    micronutrients:
      notes: "Emphasize vegetables, fruits, and whole foods for vitamins and minerals. Consider vitamin D and iron status if plant-based."
    supplements:
      notes: "Consider whey protein, creatine monohydrate, and a multivitamin if dietary intake is insufficient. Consult with a healthcare provider before starting supplements."
